lessons.title: Grammar — Modal Verbs (p. 141-142)
lessons.notes_html:
Modal verbs are auxiliary verbs used to express various degrees of necessity, possibility, ability or permission in a sentence. 1. Should/Should not: Should indicates advice, recommendation, or obligation. Example: You should wear a helmet when riding a bike. Should not indicates prohibition or advice against doing something. Example: You should not play on road. 2. Could/Couldn't: Could indicates ability, possibility, or past ability. Example: She could swim when she was younger. Couldn't indicates inability or impossibility. Example: He couldn't attend the class because he was sick. 3. Must/Mustn't: Must indicates strong obligation, necessity, or certainty. Example: You must submit your assignment by Friday. Mustn't indicates prohibition or strong

advice against doing something. Example: You must not tell a lie. 4. Can/Cannot: Can indicates ability, possibility, or permission. Example: She can speak English fluently. Cannot indicates inability or prohibition. Example: You cannot enter without permission. 5. May/May not: May indicates permission, possibility, or likelihood. Example: You may leave early if you finish your work. May not indicates prohibition or uncertainty. Example: You may not use your phone during the exam.

mcqs.q: What are modal verbs?

lessons.title: Tenses — Past Continuous Tense (p. 142-143)
lessons.notes_html:
Past Continuous Tense: The past continuous tense is used to talk about actions or events that were ongoing or in progress at a specific point in the past. Positive Sentence: Subject + was/were + verb-ing + object.

Examples: 1. I was playing with my toys. 2. She was reading a book. 3. They were watching TV. 4. He was eating dinner. Negative Sentence: Subject + was/were + not + verb-ing + object. Examples: 1. I was not sleeping. 2. She was not studying. 3. They were not dancing. 4. He was not playing outside. Interrogative Sentence: Was/Were + subject + verb-ing + object? Examples: 1. Was I running fast? 2. Was she eating breakfast? 3. Were they playing in the park? 4. Was he swimming in the pool?

options: Subject plus was/were plus verb-ing plus object
mcqs.why: Positive form is Subject plus was/were plus verb-ing plus object, as given in the tense notes.

options: I was playing with my toys
mcqs.why: I was playing with my toys is the first positive example of past continuous in the notes.

options: Were they playing in the park?
mcqs.why: They were watching TV is a positive past continuous example using were plus watching.

options: Was plus not plus subject only
Subject plus was/were plus not plus verb-ing plus object
Subject plus did not plus verb-ing
mcqs.why: Negative form adds not after was or were: subject plus was/were plus not plus verb-ing plus object.

lessons.title: Lesson text — Eid-ul-Fitr: A Celebration of Joy and Renewal (p. 147-148)
lessons.notes_html:
Eid-ul-Fitr is a very special festival for Muslims. Eid-ul-Fitr comes after the month of Ramadan on the first day of Shawal every year. During Ramadan, Muslims try to be patient, kind, and helpful. They avoid bad habits and try to do good deeds. People prepare for Eid celebrations. Many families clean their homes, buy new clothes, and decorate their houses. The night before Eid is called Chand Raat. People go to markets. Everyone feels excited for the Eid day. On Eid morning, people greet each other with happy smiles. Families visit their relatives, neighbors, and friends. Everywhere you go, people are saying 'Eid Mubarak!' It is a day full of joy and togetherness. Many families cook special food at home. Some families share food with their neighbors. This shows love and kindness in the community. Children enjoy wearing their new clothes and meeting their cousins and friends. They play games and have fun for the whole day. Eid is a reward from Allah for the Muslims. It reminds Muslims to continue good habits even after Ramadan. It teaches them to care for

others, forgive people, and stay thankful. Eid also teaches the importance of family. Spending time with parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters, and friends brings happiness. It helps everyone feel close to each other. Eid is not only about eating and having fun. It is also about sharing. Muslims give Fitrana before the Eid prayer. This money is used to help poor people. Many people also give charity, clothes, and food to those in need. When everyone shares, everyone can enjoy Eid. This makes the festival more meaningful. Festivals bring color and joy to our lives. They give us a chance to meet people, celebrate traditions, and enjoy special moments. People in Pakistan belong to different religions. Muslims celebrate Eid, Christians celebrate Christmas, Hindus celebrate Diwali, and Sikhs celebrate Vaisakhi. Pakistan is a beautiful country with people from different religions. We should respect each other's festivals. In this way, we can make our country peaceful and strong.

lessons.title: Oral Communication Skills — Engaging in role (p. 150-153)
lessons.notes_html:
play to perform a character: The Clever Rabbit and the Hungry Lion Characters: Rabbit (Clever and brave); Lion (Hungry and proud); Animals (Deer, Monkey, and Elephant - scared of the lion). Scene: A jungle where all animals are scared of the lion. Scene 1: The Jungle - In a big jungle, there lived a hungry lion. He was very strong and made all the animals afraid. Lion: (Roaring) I am the king of the jungle. Every day, one animal must come to me for my meal. Elephant: (Worried) Oh no! What will we do? Monkey: (Scared) We must think of something before he eats all of us. Deer: (Sad) We need a clever idea to stop him. Scene 2: The Clever Rabbit's Plan - The animals were very worried, but then a clever rabbit had a plan. Rabbit: (Smiling) Don't worry, friends. I know how to trick the lion. Narrator: The next day, the rabbit went to the lion very late. Lion: (Angry) Why are you late? I am very hungry. Rabbit: (Politely) Oh great lion, I was coming here, but another big lion stopped me! He said he is the real king. Lion: (Roaring) Another lion? Take me to him now. Scene 3: The Trick - The rabbit took the lion to a deep well and pointed inside. Rabbit: (Pointing) Look inside. He is down there. Lion: (Looking inside)

Grrr! I will fight him. The lion saw his own reflection in the water and thought it was another lion. Lion: (Jumping in) I will defeat you. Ahhh! (Falls into the well). Scene 4: The Happy Animals - The lion fell into the well and could not come out. The jungle was safe. Elephant: (Cheering) Hooray! The lion has gone. Monkey: (Clapping) The clever rabbit saved us all. Deer: (Smiling) Thank you, Rabbit. You are so smart. Rabbit: (Happily) Always use your mind instead of fear. Activity (page 153): Choose students to play the Rabbit, Lion, Elephant, Monkey and Deer. If there are more students, they can be extra jungle animals.

lessons.title: Requests, Exclamations and Commands (p. 155)
lessons.notes_html: 1. Requests express politeness: 'Please pass me...'. 2. Exclamations express feelings: 'Wow! That was great!'. 3. Commands express orders: 'Sit down.' lessons.title: Lesson text — Media as a Source of Learning (p. 159-160)
lessons.notes_html: Media is an amazing way for us to learn and grow. It helps us communicate and share information. This can include books, videos, TV shows, websites, and even games. Each of these can be helpful for learning and becoming a better person. Books: Books are like magical doorways that take us on great adventures and teach us new things. Storybooks have stories with pictures. Non-fiction books having facts. Reading helps us learn new words, understand different ideas, and explore new things. Videos and TV shows: Watching educational videos and shows can be a fun way to learn about science, history, nature, and much more. Internet: Internet is like a large library with vast information waiting for us to discover. Websites and online resources can help us learn about anything we are interested in. We can learn maths, language, arts and music etc by using internet. Games: We can learn from games. Puzzle games challenge our minds and adventure games help explore new things. Games can also help us learn important skills like problem-solving, creativity, and teamwork. Media is a powerful tool for learning, and by exploring books, videos, websites, and games, we can expand our knowledge, creativity, and become dedicated learners. Media plays an important role in making the world a small village.

lessons.title: Grammar — Future Tense (p. 164)
lessons.notes_html: Future Tense: Subject + will/shall + first form of the verb + object. Examples: 1. I will go to the library tomorrow. 2. My friends will come to my home tomorrow. 3. You will get first position in exam. 4. I shall meet you at the park at 3 p.m. Will/Shall: To form the future tense with 'will,' we use 'will' followed by the first form of the verb. 'Shall' is less commonly used in modern English for future tense but can still be used for suggestions, offers, or promises. It's mainly used with 'I' and 'we' subjects. 2. Be going to: To form the future tense with 'be going to,' use the appropriate form of the verb 'to be' (am/is/are) followed by 'going to' and then the first form of the verb. Subject + am/is/are + going to + first form of the verb + object. Examples: 1. My parents are going to attend the concert. 2. I am going to visit my uncle next weekend. 3. We are going to have a party on Saturday.

mcqs.why: Will followed by the first form go shows future tense in this example.

mcqs.why: Shall is mainly used with I and we subjects, according to the notes.

lessons.title: Phrases and Sentences (p. 165-166)
lessons.notes_html: Phrase: A phrase is a group of words that express a single idea or concept, but it does not contain a subject and a verb, so it does not express a complete thought or make sense on its own. Examples: 1. on the table, 2. under the bed, 3. running fast, 4. in the morning, 5. across the street. Sentence: A sentence is a group of words that contains a subject and a verb (predicate), and it expresses a complete thought or idea. Sentences can stand alone and make sense by themselves. Examples: 1. I like to play with my doll. 2. She reads books everyday. 3. They go to the park on Sundays. 4. He eats lunch at noon. 5. Birds fly in the sky. 6. The sun shines brightly.
